title: Detection and Classification in Latent Spaces: High-Dimensional Analysis and Validation
abstract: arXiv:2611.18164v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Foundation models produce high-dimensional latent representations in which suitably designed statistical decision rules can be effective yet analytically tractable. We study such detectors in the high-dimensional regime, where latent dimension and training sample size grow proportionally. For linear and quadratic statistics, we derive explicit large-deviation characterizations of false-alarm and miss-detection performance under the Neyman-Pearson paradigm, and show how the binary analysis extends to multi-class classification. The resulting error probabilities and corresponding decay rates exhibit non-monotonic dependence on the shape parameter, including double-descent and, in some regimes, multiple-descent. Experiments on vision, text, and audio datasets using modern foundation models show close agreement between theoretical predictions and empirical performance. translated_title: 潜空间中的检测与分类：高维分析与验证
translated_abstract: 基础模型会产生高维潜在表示，其中经过适当设计的统计决策规则既能有效工作，又便于解析处理。我们在高维状态下研究这类检测器，即潜在维度与训练样本规模按比例增长的情形。对于线性和二次统计量，我们在Neyman-Pearson范式下推导出了虚警与漏检性能的显式大偏差刻画，并展示了二元分析如何扩展到多类别分类。所得到的错误概率及相应的衰减速率对形状参数呈现出非单调依赖性，包括双下降现象，在某些状态下甚至出现多重下降现象。在现代基础模型上对视觉、文本和音频数据集进行的实验表明，理论预测与实际性能高度吻合。特别地，所提出的框架使我们能够设定预定的虚警……
tldr: 该论文在潜在维度与样本规模成比例增长的高维状态下，对基础模型潜空间中的线性和二次检测器进行了Neyman-Pearson大偏差分析，推导出虚警与漏检错误概率的显式刻画，揭示了双下降乃至多重下降的非单调现象，并通过视觉、文本和音频数据集实验验证了理论预测与实际性能的高度一致性。
en_tdlr: This paper provides a high-dimensional large-deviation analysis of linear and quadratic detectors in foundation-model latent spaces under the Neyman-Pearson paradigm, deriving explicit false-alarm and miss-detection characterizations that reveal double- and multiple-descent phenomena, with theoretical predictions closely validated on vision, text, and audio datasets.
